Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live''

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR PUTTING SHOTS 

( First Revision ) 



( Reaffirmed 2000 ) 



1. Scope — This standard prescribes requirements and test for putting shots for men and women. 

2. Material — The shots shall be manufactured from solid cast iron, brass or any other metal not 
softer than brass, or a shell of such metal filled with lead or other material. 

3. Mass and Diameter — As given in Table 1 .

4. Manufacture, Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The shots shall be spherical in shape. When filled, the filling shall be immovable and the centre of 
gravity shall not be more than 6 mm from the centre of the sphere. 

4.2 The shots shall not have any protruding edges and the surface shall be finished smooth. 

5. Test for Centre of Gravity — The shots shall balance on a horizontal sharp-edged circular orifice, 
12 mm in diameter, in different positions { see Fig. 1 ). 

DIA 12 mm

6. Marking — Each shot shall carry the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark. 
6.1 Standard Marliing — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards.

7. Packing — The shots shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 

8. Sampling — Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the sampling 
procedure given in IS : 2500 (Part 1 )-1973 'Sampling inspection tables : Part 1 Inspection by 
attributes and by count of defects ( first revision )', shall be followed, with the definition of lot, type of 
plan. Inspection Level and Acceptable Quality Level as given in 8.1 and 8.2. 

8.1 iof— In any consignment all putting shots of same size, manufactured from identical material 
under similar conditions Shall be grouped together to constitute a lot 

8.2 For all th6 requirements given in this specification, a single sampling plan with Inspection Level IV 
and Acceptable Quality Level 2'5 percent shall be followed. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first issued in 1967. This revision is brought out mainly to align the standard 
with the latest rules of the International Amateur Athletic Federation, as desired by the Consultative 
Committee of Parliament for the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports. The alterations made in this 
revision include modifications in requirements for mass of the putting shots.
